decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through various processing techniques and alloy design. Earlier studies have explored the effects of mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and selective laser melting on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. Recent studies have also investigated the use of high-pressure and high-temperature treatment to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in eutectic high entropy alloys.
decision.unsolved: The development of HEAs with improved magnetocaloric properties remains a challenge. While some studies have reported enhanced mechanical properties and corrosion resistance, the magnetocaloric properties of HEAs have not been extensively explored.
decision.why: Doping with magnetocaloric elements such as Gd, Dy, or Tb could potentially enhance the magnetocaloric properties of HEAs. This approach has been successfully used in other magnetocaloric materials and could be a promising next step in the development of HEAs with improved magnetocaloric properties.
